tools.name: is_vulnerable
tools.description: Check if a specific package version has known vulnerabilities. Requires an exact version: 'requests==2.31.0' for Python (the default ecosystem), or 'name@version' for other ecosystems (e.g., 'lodash@4.17.15' with ecosystem 'npm').

tools.name: list_ecosystems
tools.description: List the package ecosystems this server supports, with the default ecosystem, each ecosystem's registry, its package name format, and example names.

tools.name: lookup
tools.description: Look up a package by name and (optionally) version requirement to find which versions are available and/or have vulnerabilities. Supports multiple ecosystems via `ecosystem` (default: python).

tools.name: most_recent_not_vulnerable
tools.description: Find the most recent version of a package that has no known vulnerabilities. Supports multiple ecosystems via `ecosystem` (default: python).

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "most_recent_not_vulnerable" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Find the most recent version of a package that has no known vulnerabilities." → after: "Find the most recent version of a package that has no known vulnerabilities. Supports multiple ecosystems via `ecosystem` (default: python)."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
